text: The subject, Hamid Shah, a salaried medical sales officer with a declared monthly income of PKR 220,000, received a series of unusually large cash deposits between 1 May 2026 and 25 May 2026 that appear to be structured to avoid the reporting threshold. Over a 25‑day period he deposited nine cash amounts ranging from PKR 417,000 to PKR 1,974,000, with six deposits exceeding PKR 1.5 million – each just below the statutory cash‑transaction reporting (CTR) limit of PKR 2 million. The deposits were made at multiple branches (Saddar, DHA Phase 6, Clifton, Gulshan‑e‑Iqbal) and on different days, a pattern flagged by the typology engine (result 320 > alertThreshold 300). The subject also received a legitimate salary credit of PKR 220,000 on 2 May 2026, but the bulk of activity is cash‑based and unexplained. He declined to provide the source of the cash when asked about the extra paperwork required for deposits of PKR 2 million or more (branch note, 14 May 2026). Shortly after, the account was placed under enhanced monitoring without any customer contact. The combination of repeated high‑value cash deposits just under the CTR threshold, use of multiple branches, refusal to explain source of funds, and large outbound RTGS/IBFT payments to unrelated parties (Sheraz Traders, Crescent Imports) strongly suggests possible structuring (smurfing) to conceal illicit proceeds. This activity warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report.
